title: The Derivative: Speed at a Single Instant
logline: Average speeds over shrinking intervals settle on one number - the slope of the curve at an instant.
color_story: PRIMARY blue is the position curve and distance travelled; HIGHLIGHT yellow is the point we care about; SECONDARY teal is the second point that slides; ACCENT terracotta is the secant/tangent slope and the final result; MUTED grey is axes, braces and annotations.

scenes.title: A question about an instant
scenes.purpose: Pose the puzzle: speed at an instant seems to require dividing zero by zero.

beats.narration: How fast is something moving at one single instant, when no time passes at all?
beats.visual: Title card 'The Derivative' with the italic subtitle 'speed at a single instant', written in the centre.

beats.narration: Average speed is easy. Measure the distance covered, and divide by the time it took.
beats.visual: Clear. A horizontal road (number line 0 to 10, MUTED) across the upper half; a HIGHLIGHT dot drives from 0 to 6 leaving a PRIMARY trail; a MUTED brace labels the trail Delta d; below, the equation average speed = Delta d over Delta t is written.

beats.narration: But shrink the time interval down to a single instant, and that fraction becomes zero over zero. So what could speed at an instant even mean?
beats.visual: The trail shrinks into the dot; the equation transforms into speed at an instant = 0/0 ?, with 0/0 in ACCENT and circled.

scenes.title: Slopes of secant lines
scenes.purpose: Show that an average rate of change is the slope of a secant line.

beats.narration: Let's draw position as a curve. The height tells us the distance travelled after x seconds.
beats.visual: Heading 'Slopes of secant lines'. Axes on the left (x from 0 to 5, f(x) from 0 to 8) with a PRIMARY curve f(x) = 0.3x^2 + 0.4 drawn from left to right and labelled f(x).

beats.narration: Pick a moment x, and a moment a little later, x plus h. The line through these two points is called a secant.
beats.visual: HIGHLIGHT dot P at x = 1.5 and SECONDARY dot Q at x = 3.5 appear on the curve; a dashed MUTED run labelled h and a rise labelled Delta f form a triangle; an ACCENT secant line passes through P and Q.

beats.narration: Its slope, rise over run, is f of x plus h minus f of x, all divided by h. That's exactly the average speed over the interval.
beats.visual: On the right, the equation slope = (f(x+h) - f(x)) / h is written, then circumscribed in HIGHLIGHT.

scenes.title: Let h shrink
scenes.purpose: Watch secant slopes converge to the tangent slope and define the derivative as that limit.

beats.narration: Now slide the second point toward the first. As h shrinks, the secant line pivots, and its slope starts to settle down.
beats.visual: Heading 'Let h shrink'. Same axes and curve on the left. Q slides toward P as h goes from 2 to 0.4; the ACCENT secant pivots. On the right, live readouts h = ... and slope = ... update.

beats.narration: Zoom in close enough, and the curve itself looks like a straight line. The secant and the curve become indistinguishable.
beats.visual: h continues to 0.05, then the camera zooms into P until the curve looks straight and the secant lies along it; then zooms back out.

beats.narration: That settling value is the derivative: the limit of these slopes as h goes to zero. It is the slope of the tangent line.
beats.visual: The secant becomes the ACCENT tangent line at P; readouts fade; on the right the definition f'(x) = lim as h->0 of (f(x+h) - f(x)) / h is written with the limit in ACCENT and boxed.

scenes.title: An example: x squared
scenes.purpose: Compute a derivative from the definition and land the takeaway.

beats.narration: Let's try it with f of x equals x squared. Expanding x plus h squared, the difference on top is two x h plus h squared.
beats.visual: Heading 'An example: x squared'. Centre-left, the steps (x+h)^2 - x^2 over h = (2xh + h^2) over h appear line by line.

beats.narration: Divide by h and we're left with two x plus h. Now let h go to zero, and the slope is exactly two x.
beats.visual: Further lines = 2x + h and then h -> 0 gives 2x, with 2x boxed in ACCENT.

beats.narration: So the derivative is a new function. At every point on the parabola, it tells you the slope of the curve, the rate of change at that single instant.
beats.visual: Clear the algebra except the boxed result, which moves to the top right as f'(x) = 2x. Axes on the left with a PRIMARY parabola; an ACCENT tangent line slides along it from x = -1.5 to x = 1.5 with a HIGHLIGHT point, while a live readout shows slope = 2x matching the tangent.
